title: Current runner appends receipts
claim: validation_runner.py currently executes a shell command, captures exit code, duration, output summary, file hash-set digest, changed files, and appends a validation-receipt JSONL record.
evidence: main() runs subprocess.run and then appends the built receipt object.
relevance: The signed receipt design should preserve this useful evidence while moving canonical receipt creation into a trusted tool.

title: Current receipts are unsigned
claim: The current receipt append path writes sorted JSONL records and a file hash-set digest, but does not sign records or link them to the previous canonical receipt digest.
evidence: hash_set_digest and append_jsonl implement hashing and JSONL append without signature fields.
relevance: This is the forgery gap the proposal addresses.

title: Receipt validation is shape-only
claim: manage_jsonl.ts checks receipt id/type/status, validation evidence, truncation metadata, and timeout fallback decisions, but does not verify cryptographic signatures or hash-chain continuity.
evidence: hasValidationEvidence and validateReceiptRecords implement structural checks only.
relevance: Strict validation needs signature and chain verification beyond the current checks.

title: Cartographer already has a tool-host extension
claim: extensions/cartographer-tools.ts registers Cartographer tools through Pi extension APIs and executes project helper scripts via a common command wrapper.
relevance: A trusted cartographer_validation tool can be added in the existing extension surface.

title: Receipts are workflow state
claim: The README defines .plan/<topic>/receipts.jsonl as workflow state and describes validation receipts with command, result, duration, changed-file hashes, output summary, and validation IDs.
evidence: Clean Context Contract and example receipt documentation describe the artifact and fields.
relevance: Signed receipts should extend, not replace, the existing workflow-state contract.

title: Subagents are not validation authorities
claim: The README says Cartographer subagents consume receipts and deterministic validation results, but are not replacements for tool validation or parent orchestration.
evidence: The Cartographer subagents section states their limited role.
relevance: The trust model should classify subagents/workers as untrusted producers and trusted tools as validation authorities.

title: Pi extensions can host custom tools
claim: Pi extensions can register custom tools and run with full system permissions, so only trusted extension installations should hold signing authority.
evidence: Pi extension docs describe custom tools and warn extensions run with full system permissions.
relevance: The signing key belongs to a trusted extension/tool host, not to bash or worker-visible environment variables.

title: Mutating tools need queues
claim: Pi documentation recommends withFileMutationQueue for custom tools that mutate files because tool calls can run in parallel and concurrent writes can otherwise clobber each other.
evidence: The extension docs describe withFileMutationQueue for mutating custom tools.
relevance: Canonical receipt appends should serialize writes to .plan/<topic>/receipts.jsonl.

title: Node supports Ed25519
claim: Node.js v22 crypto documentation lists Ed25519 key support and WebCrypto signature verification support.
evidence: Context7 Node.js v22 crypto docs mention Ed25519 in generateKeyPairSync and subtle.verify documentation.
relevance: The TypeScript extension can implement public-key receipt signatures without adding a runtime dependency.

title: Canonical JSON supports signing
claim: RFC 8785 explains that hashing and signing require invariant data representation and defines deterministic JSON canonicalization with no extra whitespace and sorted object properties.
evidence: RFC 8785 abstract and detailed operation sections describe canonical JSON for cryptographic operations.
relevance: Receipt signatures should cover canonicalized payload bytes rather than incidental JSON formatting.

title: Existing checks can cover implementation
claim: package.json already defines script checks, typecheck, Python tests, TypeScript tests, and an aggregate check command.
evidence: package.json scripts include check:scripts, test:py, test:ts, test, and check.
relevance: Signed receipt implementation can plug into existing CI-like validation gates.

title: Tests must use temp roots
claim: Project instructions require tests and validation fixtures to use temporary/mock roots and avoid mutating the repository's real .plan artifacts.
evidence: AGENTS.md Testing and Temporary Artifacts section states this policy.
relevance: Signed receipt tests should use tempfile or /tmp project layouts.

title: Unsigned receipt tests currently pass
claim: tests/manage_jsonl.test.ts currently treats an unsigned validation-receipt with commands and passed status as valid.
evidence: The receipt validation test writes an unsigned validation-receipt and expects validate-file to pass.
relevance: Strict mode tests must replace or qualify this legacy happy path.
